intent: Finish the check_and_enable_services split at 100% line coverage by making the absolute root-owned paths its check libs probe redirectable, so the file-existence branches become reachable in tests. This is the follow-up commit the user chose (option b): split first with measured coverage, then a separate rewrite to close the gap.
scope: lib/tests/ — four new test files, plus services_assert.sh / services_path.sh / run_all.sh split out of the harness for the 250-line cap
Non-goal: the latent status-downgrade bug in the three unit checks, still pinned and named by the tests
Non-goal: behaviour change of any kind — the prefix is empty in production
changes: Every absolute path the check libs probe is now "${SYSROOT}/etc/..." where SYSROOT comes from SERVICES_ROOT. The prefix is deliberately NOT defaulted: the libs read ${SERVICES_ROOT?...} so an unset value is a hard error and only an explicitly empty value means the real filesystem. This matters because three commands in hosts_fix_resolved run outside `run` and are therefore not stopped by --dry-run (chattr -i on resolved.conf.d, find -delete over its *.conf, and an append to resolved.conf); with an empty default, a test that forgot to set SERVICES_ROOT would really delete this machine's resolved.conf drop-ins.
check_and_enable_services.sh exports SERVICES_ROOT="" beside its other configuration, so production paths are byte-identical to before.

The test harness points SERVICES_ROOT at a fixture tree it builds under its tmpdir, and owns PATH outright: $FAKE_BIN holds the shims and staged fake apps, $REAL_BIN a curated set of symlinks to genuine coreutils. The machine's /usr/bin is deliberately absent, because a really-installed discord and chromium otherwise make the "no target apps present" branches untestable — which they did until these tests caught it.
reset_state now also clears staged fake executables, so a present_command in one group cannot leak into a later one and make it pass for the wrong reason.
Fixed a bug in the harness's own lsattr shim: printf with a leading-dash format string parsed the dashes as options, so the immutable-attribute fixture silently produced no output at all.

verification.evidence: Byte-identical modulo the Date: line, re-run after the prefix rewrite. With SERVICES_ROOT empty the 87 rewritten paths resolve exactly as the literals did.

verification.command: sha256sum /etc/hosts /etc/nsswitch.conf /etc/systemd/resolved.conf; ls -1 /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d — before vs after the full suite
verification.evidence: No difference. This is the falsification check for a missed prefix site: the repair paths really do write, so any unprefixed one would have shown up here as an edited or deleted /etc file.
Only two hits remain, both literal /etc/hosts inside services_report.sh's usage help text, where a literal is correct.
220 assertions across 8 test files, 0 failures: apps 24, browser 34, common 27, hosts 51, report_and_fix 21, report 11, units 23, wrappers 29.

100.00% on seven of eight libs: services_common.sh 55/55, services_report.sh 27/27, services_units.sh 72/72 (was 84.51%), services_wrappers.sh 100/100, services_apps.sh 66/66, services_browser.sh 79/79. Measured against run_all.sh rather than a single test file, because services_common.sh is covered jointly by two test files that were split apart for the line cap.

verification.result: below target — kcov artifact, diagnosed not waived
verification.evidence: 86.05% (74/86); services_hosts_fix.sh 97.30% (72/74). The 14 lines are a kcov attribution artifact, not missing coverage. Falsified directly: running the suite under kcov prints '51 passed, 0 failed', so no group is skipped, and each supposedly-uncovered line is an issues+=("...") whose string can only reach stdout via the print loop below it — and a passing assertion matches that exact string (line 30 'may not be installed', 34 '/etc/hosts does not exist', 44 'not immutable', 52 'StevenBlack cache not found', 64/150 "'nsswitch'/'resolved' instance is missing or unhealthy"). Lines 102/113 and 51/70 are continuation lines of multi-line pipelines.
Exit 0, zero findings, standalone and with -x. No suppression added.

No check_and_enable_services file over 250, test files included. The harness needed splitting twice to get there (services_assert.sh, services_path.sh), and test_services_common.sh once (test_services_report_and_fix.sh).

risks: 87 rewritten path sites is the largest surface in this work, and this script runs hourly as root repairing the hosts blocking stack. The two falsification checks above are what makes a missed site detectable rather than a matter of inspection: an unprefixed path would either change the live output diff or leave a fingerprint in /etc, and neither happened.

SERVICES_ROOT is now load-bearing: a future caller that sources these libs without setting it gets a hard error rather than silently operating on the real filesystem. That is the intended direction of failure, but it does mean a new caller must set it explicitly.

The tests no longer read the state of this machine at all, so they can no longer catch a real-machine regression — that job belongs to the live output diff, which is run against the pre-split revision each time.
